verses.text: Next we turned and went up the road toward Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out with his whole army to fight us at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, "Do not be afraid of him. I have handed him over to you, with his whole army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God also handed over to us Og, king of Bashan, and his whole army. We defeated them and left no survivors.
At that time we captured all his towns. There was not one of their towns that we did not take: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, Og's kingdom in Bashan.
All these towns had high walls with gates and bars, and there were also many villages without walls.
We completely destroyed them, as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon. We destroyed every town, the men, women, and children.
But we kept all the animals and the goods from the towns as plunder for ourselves.
So at that time we took from these two Amorite kings the land east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
The people of Sidon call Mount Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.
We took all the towns on the high plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns in Og's kingdom in Bashan.

Og, king of Bashan, was the last of the Rephaim, the giants. His bed was made of iron. It is still in the Ammonite city of Rabbah. It was about four metres long and nearly two metres wide, by the usual measure.
Of the land we took over at that time, I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the land north of Aroer by the Arnon Valley, with half the hill country of Gilead and its towns.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og's kingdom, to half the tribe of Manasseh. The whole region of Argob in Bashan used to be known as a land of the Rephaim.

Jair, from the tribe of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He named these villages of Bashan after himself, Havvoth Jair, and they are still called that today.
I gave Gilead to Machir.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the land from Gilead down to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
Their land also included the Jordan Valley, with the Jordan River as its border, from Lake Galilee down to the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you: "The LORD your God has given you this land to own. But all your fighting men must cross over armed, ahead of your fellow Israelites.
Your wives, your children, and your animals, and I know you have many animals, may stay in the towns I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your fellow Israelites as he has to you, and they too take over the land the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. After that, each of you may go back to the land I have given you."
At that time I commanded Joshua: "You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you will go into.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God himself will fight for you."
At that time I begged the LORD,
"Sovereign LORD, you have only begun to show me, your servant, how great and powerful you are. What god in heaven or on earth can do the great and mighty things you do?
Please let me cross over and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan, that fine hill country and Lebanon."
But because of you, the LORD was angry with me and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, "That is enough! Do not speak to me about this again.
Go up to the top of Mount Pisgah and look west, north, south, and east. Look at the land with your own eyes, because you will not cross the Jordan.
But appoint Joshua as leader. Encourage him and make him strong, because he will lead these people across, and he will help them take over the land you will see."
So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.
